newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan province chief condemns U.S. over arrest.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan province chief condemns U.S. over arrest.

text.p: The chief minister of Pakistan's Baluchistan province condemned the U.S. and Pakistani governments on Monday over the recent arrest of a Pakistani man accused of a 1993 deadly shooting outside CIA headquarters.
"This arrest (of Mir Aimal Kansi) and his transfer to them (the United States) cannot be condemned enough," Chief Minister Akhtar Mengal told the provincial assembly.

Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government has still not explained the controversial arrest of Kansi, a native of Baluchistan, since it was announced last Tuesday by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in Washington.

Kansi, 33, is accused of killing two CIA workers and injuring three others in a shooting spree outside the spy agency's headquarters in Langley, Virginia, on January 25, 1993 before escaping to Pakistan.

Sharif's government has kept silent on the Kansi affair and is under fire from several religious and nationalist parties for its apparent collusion in the U.S.-led operation to spirit the wanted man out of Pakistan.

But opposition leader and former prime minister Benazir Bhutto on Saturday lent cautious support to Kansi's capture. Her government, forced from power last November, had also tried to arrest Kansi without success, she said in an interview with Reuters.
Kansi is reported to have been grabbed from a hotel in the Punjab provincial town of Dera Ghazi Khan in the early hours of June 15 by FBI agents, backed by Pakistani security men.
He was then flown from Islamabad to the United States in a U.S. military plane, apparently without a court hearing or any formal extradition procedures.

Mengal, who heads a coalition of several Baluchi nationalist and religious groups, accused the federal government in Islamabad of taking orders from the United States and said it might not have been informed before Kansi was actually arrested.
"There is no doubt that we carry out American orders," Mengal said. "Our foreign policy, budget and even appointments at certain government posts are made at their behest."
"The CIA is whisking away our people and our government is unaware (of) it," Mengal's senior minister Amir Zaman said.

The FBI said on Tuesday that Kansi had been delivered by unidentified Afghans and was brought back to the United States to face trial. It gave no details about the man's seizure and would not say if any of those involved would collect a reward of up to $2 million offered for the fugitive.
